title: Should You Include a Photo on Your Nigerian CV? Expert Guide 2026
excerpt: Learn whether adding your photo to your Nigerian CV helps or hurts your job prospects. Get expert advice on CV photos for the Nigerian job market.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: The question of whether to include a photo on your CV remains one of the most debated topics among Nigerian job seekers. While some believe a professional headshot adds a personal touch, others worry it might lead to discrimination. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore the pros and cons of adding photos to Nigerian CVs and help you make an informed decision.
The Current State of CV Photos in Nigeria

Unlike many Western countries where CV photos are discouraged or even illegal to request, Nigeria's job market has a more flexible approach. Many Nigerian employers still expect to see photos on CVs, particularly in certain industries. However, this practice is gradually changing as more international companies establish operations in Nigeria and local businesses adopt global hiring standards.
The decision to include a photo often depends on the industry, company culture, and specific role you're applying for. Understanding these nuances can significantly impact your job search success.
Industries Where Photos Are Still Expected
Certain sectors in Nigeria continue to favor CVs with professional photos:

items: **Banking and Finance**: Traditional banks like GTBank, First Bank, and Zenith Bank often expect professional headshots
**Hospitality and Tourism**: Hotels, restaurants, and tourism companies frequently request photos
**Retail and Customer Service**: Companies like Shoprite, SPAR, and Jumia may prefer CVs with photos for customer-facing roles
**Media and Entertainment**: TV stations, radio companies, and advertising agencies typically expect photos
**Aviation**: Airlines such as Arik Air and Air Peace often require photos for cabin crew positions
**Real Estate**: Property companies frequently request photos for sales and marketing positions

body.text: Research the company's website and LinkedIn page to see if current employees have professional photos displayed. This can give you insight into their photo expectations.
Industries Moving Away from CV Photos
Several sectors in Nigeria are adopting international best practices by focusing on skills rather than appearance:

items: **Technology and Startups**: Companies like Paystack, Flutterwave, and Andela prioritize technical skills over photos
**Oil and Gas**: International companies like Shell, ExxonMobil, and Chevron follow global anti-discrimination policies
**Multinational Corporations**: Companies like Unilever, Nestle, and PwC often discourage CV photos
**NGOs and Development Organizations**: Organizations like USAID, World Bank, and local NGOs focus on experience and qualifications
**Academic Institutions**: Universities and research institutions typically don't require photos

body.text: Advantages of Including a Photo on Your Nigerian CV
When done correctly, a professional photo can offer several benefits:

**Creates Personal Connection**: A friendly, professional photo can help recruiters remember you among hundreds of applications. Nigerian hiring managers often appreciate being able to put a face to the qualifications.
**Shows Professionalism**: A high-quality headshot demonstrates attention to detail and investment in your professional image.
**Cultural Expectations**: Meeting traditional expectations in conservative industries can work in your favor, especially with older hiring managers.
**Networking Advantage**: When attending job fairs or networking events in Lagos, Abuja, or Port Harcourt, having a recognizable photo on your CV helps people remember your conversations.
Disadvantages and Risks of CV Photos
Including a photo also carries potential drawbacks:
**Unconscious Bias**: Despite best intentions, recruiters may make decisions based on appearance, age, ethnicity, or perceived social class rather than qualifications.
**Discrimination Concerns**: Photos can lead to unfair treatment based on factors unrelated to job performance, including gender, tribal affiliation, or physical appearance.
**ATS Compatibility Issues**: Many modern Applicant Tracking Systems used by Nigerian companies struggle to process images, potentially causing your CV to be filtered out automatically.
**Professional Image Risks**: Poor-quality photos or inappropriate images can harm your chances more than help them.
**Space Consumption**: Photos take up valuable CV real estate that could be used for relevant skills, experience, or achievements.
Best Practices for CV Photos in Nigeria
If you decide to include a photo, follow these professional guidelines:
Photo Quality Standards

items: Use a high-resolution image (at least 300 DPI)
Ensure proper lighting with no shadows on your face
Choose a neutral, professional background (white or light grey)
Maintain sharp focus on your face and shoulders
Keep the photo recent (within the last two years)

body.text: Styling and Appearance

items: Dress in professional business attire appropriate for your target industry
For men: suit and tie or professional shirt with blazer
For women: business suit, professional blouse, or conservative dress
Ensure neat, professional grooming
Smile naturally but maintain a professional demeanor
Make direct eye contact with the camera

body.text: Technical Specifications

items: Size: 2x2 inches or passport photo dimensions
Format: JPEG or PNG
File size: Under 1MB for easy uploading
Position: Top right corner of your CV header

body.text: Consider getting professional headshots taken at photography studios in major Nigerian cities like Lagos (Victoria Island, Ikoyi), Abuja (Wuse, Garki), or Port Harcourt. Many offer affordable packages specifically for job seekers.
Alternative Strategies for Nigerian Job Seekers
If you're unsure about including a photo, consider these alternatives:
**Create Two CV Versions**: Maintain one version with a professional photo and another without. Use the appropriate version based on the company and role.
**Research Company Culture**: Check the organization's website, social media presence, and employee profiles on LinkedIn to gauge their photo expectations.
**Industry-Specific Approach**: Follow industry norms while remaining flexible for companies that explicitly state their preferences.
**Focus on Digital Presence**: Ensure your LinkedIn profile has a professional photo, allowing recruiters to see your image if they choose to look you up.
Modern Trends in Nigerian Recruitment
The Nigerian job market is evolving, with several trends affecting photo inclusion:
**Digital Transformation**: More companies are using ATS software that may not process photos effectively, especially smaller businesses upgrading their hiring processes.
**Diversity and Inclusion**: Forward-thinking Nigerian companies are implementing bias-reduction strategies in their hiring processes.
**Remote Work Culture**: The rise of remote work, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, has shifted focus toward skills and qualifications over physical appearance.
**International Standards**: As Nigeria integrates more deeply into the global economy, local companies are adopting international recruitment best practices.
Making Your Decision: A Framework
Use this decision framework to determine whether to include a photo:
**Step 1: Research the Company**

items: Check if they're local or international
Review their website and social media for diversity messaging
Look at employee photos on their platforms

body.text: **Step 2: Consider the Industry**

items: Traditional industries may expect photos
Tech and international companies often don't
Customer-facing roles might benefit from photos

body.text: **Step 3: Evaluate the Role**

items: Senior executive positions typically don't need photos
Entry-level positions in traditional sectors might
Remote roles rarely require photos

body.text: **Step 4: Assess Your Comfort Level**

items: Only include a photo if you're comfortable with it
Consider potential bias but don't let fear paralyze you
Trust your instincts about the company culture

Final Recommendations

The decision to include a photo on your Nigerian CV should be strategic rather than automatic. Consider your target industry, the specific companies you're applying to, and your personal comfort level. Remember that your qualifications, experience, and skills matter most in securing interviews and job offers.

As Nigeria's job market continues to evolve, staying flexible and informed about current trends will serve you well. Whether you choose to include a photo or not, ensure your CV is professionally written, ATS-optimized, and tailored to each application.

Focus on creating a compelling narrative of your professional journey, highlighting achievements with quantifiable results, and demonstrating how you can add value to potential employers. In the end, a well-crafted CV with or without a photo will always outperform a mediocre one, regardless of how professional the headshot might be.
